title: Data residency & compliance discovery - Ashfield Bank
summary: Intro discovery focused on whether Redwood hosted/Dedicated/Private options meet Ashfield Bank's data residency and compliance needs. Key topics: EU data residency, HIPAA/financial controls, audit logging, customer-managed keys, and limited logging for PII. Agreed next steps: send SOC2/HIPAA docs, schedule technical deep dive on VPC peering and network egress, and prepare a pricing sketch for Dedicated and Private options.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Time: 16:30 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood CSM), Mark Davenport (Ashfield CISO), Elena Ruiz (Ashfield Head of Cloud), Samir Patel (Ashfield Compliance), Tina O'Leary (Ashfield DevOps)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our SE and Carlos from success. How are you all?
[00:08] Mark Davenport: Good, thanks Jordan. Big day for us, we want to understand options - hosted, dedicated, private - and what meets our regs.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: Totally. Quick agenda: we wanna cover high-level compliance posture, where you need data to live, KMS/HSM needs, logging and retention, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:23] Elena Ruiz: Yep. Also network connectivity - we need to know if we can peer into our VPC or if traffic goes over public egress.
[00:30] Priya Nair: Great, we'll walk through each model. Just to call out, Redwood Hosted is our SaaS API with options for region pinning, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in a customer-tenant environment, and Private is a customer-managed control plane - the most isolated option.
[00:45] Samir Patel: First question - GDPR and EU residency. We have retail ops in the EU; any EU data has to remain in EU. Can Redwood guarantee that for hosted?
[00:53] Jordan Lee: For Hosted we have regional endpoints, and we can pin tenancy to EU regions. However, logs and some observability may still pass through central services unless we set up a Private deployment. For strict legal residency we usually recommend Private or Dedicated deployed in customer's chosen region with data plane restricted.
[01:10] Mark Davenport: Okay can you clarify what's stored in logs - request bodies, prompts, responses? We cannot have sensitive PII in logs for some workflows.
[01:18] Priya Nair: By default we capture metadata (request IDs, latency, model used) and token counts. Full transcript logging is opt-in - on Hosted account level it's typically available for debugging but we offer log redaction and retention controls. For Dedicated and Private, you can disable storing request/response payloads and keep only minimal operational logs.
[01:35] Tina O'Leary: Wait, when you say disable - is that a config flag or does it require code changes? We need to ensure devs can't accidentally log.
[01:40] Priya Nair: It's a deployment configuration, not a runtime flag in the client SDK; for Dedicated and Private it's an admin config. For Hosted we'll work with you - you can opt out of retention and enable redaction, but for absolute control Private is the cleanest.
[01:55] Elena Ruiz: KMS - we need customer-supplied keys, HSM-backed. Do you support BYOK?
[02:01] Jordan Lee: Yes, we support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest across Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we support KMS integration per region and in some enterprise cases bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via HSM integrations. We'll send the key rotation/management docs.
[02:15] Samir Patel: HIPAA - we have a small set of workflows that fall under payments-embedded health data, weird, but still applicable. Are you willing to sign a BAA and do you have HIPAA controls?
[02:25] Jordan Lee: We have HIPAA controls and have signed BAAs with existing customers. We'll share attestation artifacts. Note: Hosted can be used under BAA if we configure logging and retention per your policies; again Private offers the least shared-surface.
[02:42] Mark Davenport: On auditing - we need immutable audit logs for access to data, model changes, and admin actions. Are those available and can they ship to our SIEM?
[02:51] Priya Nair: Yes, audit logs are available. For Dedicated/Private you can push logs to your SIEM via syslog or to a secure S3 with object lock for immutability. For Hosted we can forward logs via a customer-managed endpoint (e.g., private link or syslog over TLS). Some setup needed for guaranteed immutability but it's doable.
[03:10] Elena Ruiz: Network egress - can we avoid public internet for model calls? We prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink.
[03:16] Priya Nair: Dedicated supports VPC peering and cross-VPC routing. Private supports deployment entirely inside your VPC - no public egress. Hosted supports PrivateLink in select regions. We'll map the options in the tech deep dive.
[03:30] Mark Davenport: Any third-party subprocessors? We need a list for our legal review.
[03:34] Jordan Lee: We maintain a subprocessors list; major cloud infra providers, monitoring vendors - we'll attach the latest list to the SOC2 package.
[03:42] Samir Patel: Regarding data retention windows, we need the ability to retain logs for X years and delete request payloads after Y days. Is that configurable per customer?
[03:51] Priya Nair: Yes, retention windows are configurable. On Hosted there's a management UI and API for retention policies. Dedicated/Private give you full control in config and S3 lifecycle rules. The only nuance is analytics and aggregated metrics which, if you want, can be disabled or exported without payloads.
[04:10] Tina O'Leary: A practical question - if we go with Dedicated, what changes do we need on our side? How long to provision and what's the network setup?
[04:18] Priya Nair: Typical Dedicated provisioning is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and approvals. You'll need a VPC for peering, appropriate routing, and a small set of firewall rules. We'll provide Terraform/CloudFormation templates. For Private, timeline is longer (4-8 weeks) because it can include on-prem packaging.
[04:34] Jordan Lee: Also, cost tradeoffs: Hosted is fastest and cheapest to start, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, Private for strict compliance. We'll send a pricing sketch.
[04:44] Mark Davenport: About model variants - if you have fallback models, do we get logs when the system falls back? We don't want user data sent to different regions unknowingly.
[04:52] Priya Nair: Fallbacks are configured by policy. We can restrict fallbacks to the same region or the same tenancy. We'll document model routing policies; default is locality-preserving.
[05:05] Samir Patel: One more on redaction - do you do automated PII detection and redaction in logs? Or do we run a preprocess?
[05:12] Priya Nair: We offer an automated redaction layer that can remove or hash detected PII from logs; it's heuristic and configurable. For high-assurance workflows we recommend client-side redaction (in your app) combined with server-side redaction.
[05:25] Elena Ruiz: Ok good. Are there any limitations for embeddings or vector stores - like content leaving EU to US for index building?
[05:31] Jordan Lee: Embeddings and derived artifacts follow the data plane residency rules. If you want indices to stay in EU, we can pin storage and compute to EU in Dedicated/Private. Hosted needs to be region-pinned; some managed services for embeddings may cross-region unless configured. We'll clarify exactly how vector stores are handled.
[05:50] Carlos Mendes: For the next steps we should schedule a technical deep dive with your infra folks to go through VPC peering, KMS, and log routing. Also Jordan will send legal/security pack.
[05:59] Mark Davenport: That sounds right. I'd like to add a pilot success criteria: 100% EU residency for EU users, zero retention of PII in logs, and audit log forwarding to our SIEM. If we meet that in pilot we'll look at Dedicated/Private procurement.
[06:14] Jordan Lee: Great - we'll take that as the success criteria. Anything else?
[06:18] Tina O'Leary: One more - how do you handle incident response and notification for security events?
[06:23] Priya Nair: We have incident response SLAs for Dedicated/Private customers and will integrate with your pager or Slack for high-severity incidents. We'll include our IR playbook in the docs.
[06:34] Mark Davenport: Alright let's wrap. Recap: Jordan send SOC2/HIPAA/ISO artifacts and subprocessors list; Priya schedule SE deep dive focusing on VPC, KMS, logging; Carlos send Private/Dedicated architecture sample; Ashfield to send their compliance checklist.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: Perfect, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email, and Priya will propose times for next week.
[06:56] Elena Ruiz: Thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional transcription errors: "K V cash" instead of KV cache, "Private link" sometimes transcribed as "private linke", small punctuation issues.
